final_answer:
once upon a time, in a lush green valley, lived a tortoise named terry. unlike his kin, terry dreamed of soaring through the skies, not crawling along the ground. each morning, he would gaze at the birds and whisper, “one day, i will fly.” his friends laughed, saying, “you’re too slow, too heavy. flying is for the swift and light.” but terry refused to let their words dim his hope.  

terry spent months studying the birds, observing their wings and flight patterns. he tried gliding off cliffs, but gravity always pulled him back. he crafted wings from leaves and feathers, yet they crumpled under his weight. discouraged, he nearly gave up—until a wise old owl perched nearby. “flying isn’t about strength or speed,” the owl said. “it’s about believing in yourself, even when the world doubts you.”  

inspired, terry practiced endlessly, adjusting his wings, learning to balance, and building stamina. one day, as a storm raged, he leapt from a high rock, wings flapping wildly. the wind caught him, and against all odds, he soared! the valley cheered as terry danced through the clouds, proving that dreams are not bound by limits.  

moral: true success lies not in what others deem possible, but in the courage to chase your own sky.
